doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Left behind by Nat Towles in Iowa
summary: Tate and Henry Coker were stranded by Nat Towles, got their money back through a police captain, and went on to Omaha.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Do you have a funny little story about the Basie band that you could leave us with? Or anything that happened? Al asked me to talk to you about one night that you and another player got lost or got left behind or something on a trip?

No, I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times because Towl would leave sometimes and it wouldn’t be nobody but him. If we was supposed to leave at a certain time he would leave, and he left us, left me and Henry Coker, who later became a great trombone player man, and he left us in DesMoines, Iowa or somewhere. And we went out and picked pockets, somebody picked pockets, and we got our money back and more. I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

learned. And I tried to pull Coker’s coat you know, because I had seen this happen. You know whatever you say you get pickpocket, you had to make it good, so and I knew this and I had seen this happen you know? So I think we got pickpocket for about $15 apiece, but no money man, you know? So we wake up and everybody’s gone and the money’s gone, and when I went to the landlord of the house and told him that we didn’t have any money and what have you. So he cursed us out and everything. So I says okay. So I went on down to the police station and the policeman, the captain there was a trumpet player. He says, “I know where you were.” See he called the name of the house, he says, “come on.” And he put us in a corner and carried us back in there, and they were sitting around in there gambling and having a good time. He went in and he says “now I let you all operate, gamble, do everything you want, but when you start that stealing, I’ll close your house down right now.” So and he says, “what did you say you lost?” I said, “$30.” I say, “he did too.” He says, “no I ain’t lose but $15.” I said, “you had the same thing I did.” I kept it right up there. He says, “no I didn’t have but $15.” But I laughed.
Allow for a little inflation, huh?

So they give us that money so the policeman says, “now what do you all want to do, do you want to stay here or do you want us to take you to the train station?” I says, “I want you to take us to the bus station and stay with us until that bus gets rid of me. Because I know them cats man, and I know them cats will send somebody after us.” So they put us on the bus and we went on to Omaha. And I wouldn’t speak to Towles no more, I didn’t speak to him for about a week and I wouldn’t play with him or anything like that because he’s wild, from Memphis, you know.
